docs.title: PhpDatabase
docs.text:
PhpDatabase is a pure PHP library to read and write database documents.

Format Extension Read Write Notes Microsoft Access 2007+ .accdb ✅ ✅ Jet/ACE pages, memo/OLE long values, Unicode compression, indexes, relationships, properties Microsoft Access 2000-2003 .mdb ✅ ✅ Jet 4 (Access 97/Jet 3 is not supported) OpenDocument Database (LibreOffice Base) .odb ✅ ✅ embedded HSQLDB 1.8 database: MEMORY and CACHED tables SQLite 3 .sqlite, .sqlite3, .db ✅ ✅ B-trees, overflow pages, WITHOUT ROWID tables, UTF-8/UTF-16, WAL file

No database engine, PDO driver or zip extension is needed: the files are read and written by the library itself (ODB packages through PclZip, with phpoffice/common). Only dom, mbstring and zlib are required.

The features supported by each reader and writer (versions, storage, schema, data types, document properties) are listed in features.md; format internals are described in formats.md.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: composer require phpoffice/phpdatabase

docs.title: Create a database
docs.text:
use PhpOffice\PhpDatabase\ColumnType;
use PhpOffice\PhpDatabase\Database;
use PhpOffice\PhpDatabase\ForeignKey;
use PhpOffice\PhpDatabase\IOFactory;

$database = new Database();
$database->getDocumentProperties()->setTitle('Library');

$books = $database->createTable('Books');
$books->createColumn('ID', ColumnType::INTEGER)->setPrimaryKey()->setAutoIncrement();
$books->createColumn('Title', ColumnType::TEXT, 200)->setNullable(false);
$books->createColumn('Price', ColumnType::DECIMAL)->setPrecision(8, 2);
$books->createColumn('Published', ColumnType::DATE);
$books->createColumn('Available', ColumnType::BOOLEAN)->setDefaultValue(true);
$books->createColumn('Cover', ColumnType::BLOB);

$books->addRow(['Title' => 'Les Misérables', 'Price' => '12.90', 'Published' => '1862-04-03']);
$books->addRow([null, 'Germinal', 8.2, new DateTimeImmutable('1885-03-01'), false, null]); // list in the column order

$authors = $database->createTable('Authors');
$authors->createColumn('ID', ColumnType::INTEGER)->setPrimaryKey()->setAutoIncrement();
$authors->createColumn('Name', ColumnType::TEXT, 100)->setDescription('Full name');
$books->createColumn('AuthorID', ColumnType::INTEGER);
$books->createIndex('BooksTitle', ['Title']);                       // unique: createIndex(..., true)
$books->createForeignKey(['AuthorID'], 'Authors', ['ID'], 'BooksAuthors')
    ->setOnDelete(ForeignKey::CASCADE);

$writer = IOFactory::createWriter($database, 'Accdb'); // Accdb, Odb, Sqlite
$writer->save('library.accdb');

docs.title: Read a file
docs.text:
use PhpOffice\PhpDatabase\IOFactory;
use PhpOffice\PhpDatabase\Reader\ReaderInterface;

$database = IOFactory::load('library.odb');          // format detected from the content
// or: IOFactory::createReader('Odb')->load('library.odb', ReaderInterface::SKIP_ROWS);

foreach ($database->getTables() as $table) {
    echo $table->getName(), ': ', $table->getRowCount(), ' rows', PHP_EOL;
    foreach ($table->getColumns() as $column) {
        echo '  ', $column->getName(), ' ', $column->getType(), $column->isPrimaryKey() ? ' (PK)' : '', PHP_EOL;
    }
    foreach ($table->getRows() as $row) {
        echo '  ', $row['Title'], PHP_EOL;
    }
}

docs.title: Views, constraints and expressions
docs.text:
The SQL of views, check constraints, partial indexes and default expressions is written in standard SQL ("identifier", 'text', ||, DATE '2024-01-31', CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, LIMIT n); each writer converts it to the dialect of its format (SQLite, HSQLDB, Access: [identifier], "text", &, #2024-01-31#, Now(), TOP n).

use PhpOffice\PhpDatabase\Expression;
use PhpOffice\PhpDatabase\Index;

$books->getColumn('Price')->setDefaultValue(0);
$books->createColumn('Added', ColumnType::DATETIME)->setDefaultValue(Expression::currentTimestamp());
$books->createCheck('"Price" >= 0');
$books->addIndex(new Index('BooksByPrice', ['Price' => 'DESC', 'Title' => 'ASC']));
$books->addIndex((new Index('BooksCheap', ['Title']))->setWhere('"Price" < 10'));      // SQLite only
$books->addIndex(new Index('BooksLower', [new Expression('lower("Title")')]));        // SQLite only
$database->createView('CheapBooks', 'SELECT "Title", "Price" FROM "Books" WHERE "Price" < 10');
$database->createTrigger('BooksAudit', 'Books', 'CREATE TRIGGER ...');              // SQLite only

$writer = IOFactory::createWriter($database, 'Odb');
$writer->save('library.odb');
print_r($writer->getWarnings()); // objects the format can't hold (here: the SQLite only indexes and the trigger)

docs.title: Convert
docs.text:
IOFactory::save(IOFactory::load('legacy.mdb'), 'legacy.sqlite');   // writer chosen from the extension
IOFactory::save(IOFactory::load('data.sqlite'), 'data.odb');

docs.title: Access file format
docs.text:
use PhpOffice\PhpDatabase\Writer\Accdb;

(new Accdb($database))->setFormat(Accdb::FORMAT_ACCDB_2016)->save('data.accdb'); // BIGINT as "Large Number"
// FORMAT_MDB_2000, FORMAT_ACCDB_2007 (default for .accdb), FORMAT_ACCDB_2010, FORMAT_ACCDB_2016,
// FORMAT_ACCDB_2019 ("Date/Time Extended" for the columns with setFractionalSeconds(7))

docs.title: Object model
docs.text:
• Database: the document (like PhpPresentation), with DocumentProperties, tables, views and triggers.
  • Table: name, description, columns, rows, indexes, foreign keys, check constraints, WITHOUT ROWID (SQLite). A row is an array indexed by column name, holding PHP values.
  • Column: name, type, length, precision/scale, nullable, primary key, auto-increment, default value (a value or an Expression), description, fractional seconds digits, multi-valued (Access).
  • Index: name, columns (with their sort direction, or an Expression), unique, WHERE condition.
  • CheckConstraint: expression (standard SQL), name.
  • View: name, SELECT statement (standard SQL), description. Access select and union queries are read as views.
  • Trigger: name, table, complete CREATE TRIGGER statement (SQLite).
  • Attachment: file of an Access attachment column (name, data, type, modification date).
  • ForeignKey: name, columns, referenced table and columns, ON DELETE / ON UPDATE actions (NO ACTION, CASCADE, SET NULL, SET DEFAULT, RESTRICT).
  • ColumnType: the logical types and their PHP values:
ColumnType PHP value SQLite HSQLDB (ODB) Access BOOLEAN bool BOOLEAN (0/1) BOOLEAN Yes/No TINYINT, SMALLINT, INTEGER, BIGINT int TINYINT... TINYINT... Byte, Integer, Long Integer, Large Number (2016) FLOAT, DOUBLE float REAL, DOUBLE REAL, DOUBLE Single, Double DECIMAL numeric string DECIMAL(p,s) DECIMAL(p,s) Decimal, Currency for DECIMAL(19,4) TEXT string VARCHAR(n) / TEXT VARCHAR(n) Short Text (≤ 255), Long Text above LONGTEXT string TEXT LONGVARCHAR Long Text (memo) DATE, TIME, DATETIME DateTimeImmutable ISO 8601 text DATE, TIME, TIMESTAMP Date/Time BLOB binary string BLOB LONGVARBINARY OLE Object GUID string ({XXXXXXXX-...}) GUID (text) CHAR(38) Replication ID HYPERLINK string HYPERLINK TEXT LONGVARCHAR Hyperlink ATTACHMENT Attachment[] file names (text) file names (text) read; written as text

A multi-valued column (Column::setMultiValued()) holds a list of values: read from Access, written as text ("a; b") by all the writers.

Values given to Table::addRow() are converted to these PHP types ('abc' for an INTEGER column throws an InvalidArgumentException). Auto-increment columns get the next value when they are null.

docs.title: Limits
docs.text:
• Access: generated files are validated with Jackcess (reading, index lookups, relationships with cascades, inserting rows, creating tables) and this library's reader. They have not been tested in Microsoft Access. They are built from empty databases created by Access (see NOTICE), like Jackcess does.
  • Access: select and union queries are read and written as views; the other queries (action, crosstab, data definition, pass-through, with parameters), forms, reports and macros are not. Check constraints are combined in the validation rule of the table. Attachments and multi-valued fields are read, but written as text. Calculated columns (Access 2010) are read as plain values (their decimals with 18 digits after the point), their expression is not. Dates keep microseconds (the 7th digit of the extended date/time is lost). SET DEFAULT and RESTRICT are written as "no action". Encrypted or password protected databases (Office crypto) are not supported.
  • ODB: only the embedded HSQLDB engine is supported (not Firebird, not external data sources). Tables are written as MEMORY tables, which LibreOffice opens like the CACHED tables it creates. A foreign key is written only when the referenced columns are a primary key or a unique index (required by HSQLDB). HSQLDB 1.8 has no partial/expression indexes nor triggers, no descending index columns; views are written only when HSQLDB can load them (an invalid view prevents the whole database from opening). The database/log file of an unclosed database is replayed. Dates of the CACHED tables are stored by HSQLDB in the time zone of the Java VM: they are read in the default time zone of PHP.
  • SQLite: the -wal file next to the database is applied when reading (committed frames only). Virtual tables are not read nor written. Expression and partial indexes are written for the expressions handled by the evaluator of the library (SQLite semantics: operators, CASE, CAST, lower, substr...). Index names are global in SQLite: they must be unique in the database. Values not matching the declared type of their column are read as null.
  • Files are read in memory: very large databases need some memory.

docs.title: Formats
docs.text: The features supported by each reader and writer are listed in features.md.

docs.title: SQL of the model
docs.text:
Views, check constraints, partial indexes, expression indexes and default expressions hold standard SQL ("identifier", 'text', ||, DATE 'yyyy-mm-dd', CURRENT_DATE/TIME/TIMESTAMP, LIMIT n [OFFSET m]). Shared/Sql/Dialect converts it from and to each format:

Standard SQLite HSQLDB 1.8 Access "Name" "Name" "Name" (every identifier quoted: HSQLDB folds unquoted names to upper case) [Name] 'text', a \|\| b same same "text", a & b DATE '2024-01-31' '2024-01-31' same #2024-01-31# CURRENT_TIMESTAMP same same Now() (Date(), Time()) LIKE 'a%_' same same Like "a*?" x % 2 same same x Mod 2 LIMIT n OFFSET m same SELECT LIMIT m n ... SELECT TOP n ... (no offset)

The SQLite writer computes the entries of the partial and expression indexes with Writer/Sqlite/Evaluator, which follows the semantics of SQLite (integer division, ASCII only lower/upper, NULL propagation).

docs.title: SQLite 3
docs.text:
Reference: Database File Format.

  • The schema (sqlite_schema) is parsed with a SQL tokenizer; the declared types are mapped with the affinity rules of SQLite.
  • The writer builds 4 KB pages (Writer\Sqlite::setPageSize()): table b-trees, overflow pages and the index b-trees of the primary key (when it is not an INTEGER PRIMARY KEY) and of the indexes. Foreign keys are written in CREATE TABLE (PRAGMA foreign_keys is off by default in SQLite).
  • Views and triggers are rows of sqlite_schema (root page 0); WITHOUT ROWID tables are index b-trees whose records start with the primary key; descending index columns are stored in descending order (schema format 4).
  • The reader applies the write-ahead log (<file>-wal): the checksums of the frames are verified and only the frames up to the last commit are used, like SQLite does when it opens the database.
  • Generated files pass PRAGMA integrity_check.

docs.title: ODB (LibreOffice Base)
docs.text:
An ODB file is a ZIP package (mimetype, content.xml, META-INF/manifest.xml...), read and written with PclZip (the ZIP adapter of phpoffice/common), holding the files of an HSQLDB 1.8 database in database/:

  • script: SQL statements: CREATE TABLE, SET TABLE ... INDEX (roots of the indexes of the CACHED tables), rows of the MEMORY tables (INSERT INTO). Non ASCII characters are written as \uXXXX.
  • data: rows of the CACHED tables (the default of LibreOffice). Each row holds one AVL node per index; the reader walks the tree of the primary index from its root.
  • properties: settings of the engine.
  • log: statements executed since the last checkpoint, when the database was not closed properly (/*Cn*/ session prefix, INSERT, DELETE, DDL, COMMIT, SET AUTOCOMMIT...; an update is a DELETE followed by an INSERT). The reader replays it like HSQLDB: the transactions not committed at the end of the log are dropped.

Queries saved by LibreOffice Base are in content.xml (db:queries): they are read as views.

The writer creates MEMORY tables, an identity column for an auto-increment integer primary key and ALTER TABLE ... RESTART WITH for its next value, CREATE [UNIQUE] INDEX and ALTER TABLE ... ADD CONSTRAINT ... FOREIGN KEY (HSQLDB checks the references only when rows are inserted later, not when it loads the script), table level CHECK constraints (HSQLDB 1.8 refuses column level ones) and CREATE VIEW. HSQLDB refuses to open a database whose script holds an invalid statement: the views are written only when they use the functions and syntax of HSQLDB 1.8 and reference existing tables. Generated databases are validated by opening them with HSQLDB 1.8.0.10 (the engine embedded in LibreOffice).

docs.title: Access (ACCDB, MDB)
docs.text:
The Jet 4 (Access 2000-2003) and ACE (Access 2007-2019) formats use 4 KB pages:

  • page 0: header, partly RC4-encoded with a fixed key (version, code page, sort order, creation date);
  • MSysObjects (table definition on page 2): catalog of the tables, containers and system objects;
  • table definitions (TDEF pages, possibly chained): columns, real and logical indexes, usage maps;
  • data pages: rows (null mask, fixed columns, variable columns and their offsets);
  • LVAL pages: memo and OLE values larger than 64 bytes;
  • index pages: B-tree nodes and leaves (entry masks, encoded keys);
  • usage maps: inline bitmaps or reference maps listing the pages owned by a table.

Encoded Jet 4 databases (RC4 page encoding) are read. Access 2010+ encryption is not supported.

The writer starts from an empty database created by Access (src/PhpDatabase/Resources/Access/: one per version, like Jackcess): its pages are kept, the user tables are appended, and the rows describing them are added to the system tables MSysObjects, MSysACEs and MSysRelationships, whose indexes are written again. The global usage map (free pages) is updated.

  • Indexes: primary key, secondary indexes and the indexes of the relationships, for all the indexable types. Text keys use the "General Legacy" (Access 2000-2007) or "General" (2010+) sort order, with the code tables of Jackcess.
  • Relationships: a row of MSysRelationships per column, with referential integrity when the referenced columns are unique, and cascade updates/deletes or "set null".
  • Properties (LvProp column of MSysObjects): description of the tables and columns, Required, DefaultValue (literal or expression such as Now()), ValidationRule of the table (check constraints); title, author and comments of the database (SummaryInfo).
  • Queries: a row of MSysObjects (type 5, flags: 0 select, 128 union) and one row of MSysQueries per element of the statement (Shared/Access/QueryFormat): type, flags (DISTINCT, TOP), tables, columns, joins, WHERE, GROUP BY, HAVING, ORDER BY; for a union, the SQL of its two parts.
  • Types: GUID (Replication ID), hyperlink (memo with the hyperlink flag), "Date/Time Extended" of Access 2019 (42 ASCII bytes: days since 0001-01-01, seconds and 100 ns units; written with FORMAT_ACCDB_2019), descending index columns.
  • The sort order of the text indexes is the one of the template ("General Legacy" for Access 2000-2007 and for the Access 2019 template, "General" for 2010 and 2016).

Read only:

  • Attachments and multi-valued fields (complex columns): the values are rows of a hidden "flat" table (MSysComplexColumns); the file of an attachment is stored zlib compressed with a header holding its type. The version history of the "append only" memo columns is skipped.
  • Calculated columns (Access 2010): the type of the values is the ResultType property, each value is wrapped in a header of 20 bytes.

Generated files are validated with Jackcess: reading, lookups through the indexes (also descending, GUID and extended date indexes), referential integrity and cascades, queries (Query.toSQLString()), rows inserted and tables created afterwards by Jackcess. They have not been opened in Microsoft Access.
